cubes.description: Assessment scores across internal Illuminate interims, NJ/FL state assessments, and vendor benchmarks (i-Ready, DIBELS, STAR) — row-level (one row per student x assessment x administration x response type) and aggregate breakdowns in a single view. pct_proficient (mastery rate) is the source-agnostic headline; scale_score is null for internal rows and percent_correct is null for state and vendor rows. response_type / response_type_code carry the standard/skill breakdown (Illuminate only). State and vendor administrations have no single administered date, so the Date members (academic_year, academic_year_label, date_day, month_number, month_name) resolve for every source but are scoped by different dates per source: the administration date for Illuminate/college, the student's completion (test) date for state/vendor. A cross-source date cut (e.g. "scores in May") therefore mixes those two date concepts. Contains direct student identifiers — see access_policy for PII gating.

measures.description: Every assessment row, including the Illuminate not_taken rows where a student was assigned an assessment and never sat it. This is the widest of the three counts and the denominator for pct_taken. For assessments actually sat use count_taken; for the population pct_proficient is computed over use count_scored. COUNT(*) over the unique PK (assessment_score_key) — additive, so pre-aggregations roll it up to any grain.
measures.name: student_assessment_scores_view.count_assigned
measures.title: Student Assessment Scores View Count Assigned

measures.description: Assessments a student actually sat — every row except the Illuminate not_taken placeholders. Use this for "how many assessments were taken". It is wider than count_scored: a student can sit an assessment that carries no proficiency verdict, which is most STAR kindergarten and Early Literacy rows and the DIBELS K-2 phonics subtests. Only Illuminate can express non-participation, so for every other source this equals count_assigned.
measures.name: student_assessment_scores_view.count_taken
measures.title: Student Assessment Scores View Count Taken

measures.description: Assessments carrying a proficiency verdict (is_mastery set) — the narrowest of the three counts and the denominator pct_proficient is computed over. A row with no verdict cannot enter the numerator, so counting it would only drag the rate down. Narrower than count_taken by the rows that were sat but cannot be judged: STAR publishes no proficiency benchmark for kindergarten at any subject or for Early Literacy at any grade, and the DIBELS K-2 phonics subtests have no benchmark level set upstream. Report this alongside pct_proficient whenever the rate carries weight — it is the n the rate rests on, and it is not count_assigned.
measures.name: student_assessment_scores_view.count_scored
measures.title: Student Assessment Scores View Count Scored

measures.description: Distinct students (per student-year) with a score in the filtered slice. Exact count_distinct — non-additive, so a rollup pre-aggregation cannot re-aggregate it to a coarser grain; switch to count_distinct_approx (HLL) if/when this is pre-aggregated and an approximate distinct is acceptable.
measures.name: student_assessment_scores_view.count_students
measures.title: Student Assessment Scores View Count Students

measures.description: Grain: recomputes at any query grain, but meaningful only within Illuminate — pooling it across sources is a silent-failure trap (numerically valid, semantically meaningless). Participation rate — assessments sat / assessments assigned. Only Illuminate records non-participation, so every other source reads exactly 100% by construction rather than by fact, and a pooled cross-source rate is diluted by sources that cannot express a no-show. Filter assessment_type to illuminate before reporting this. Built from additive primitives (count_taken / count_assigned) so pre-aggregations roll it up to any grain.
measures.name: student_assessment_scores_view.pct_taken
measures.title: Student Assessment Scores View Pct Taken

measures.description: Proficiency/mastery rate — proficient scores / scores carrying a proficiency verdict. The headline, source-agnostic metric (the only score measure comparable across the incompatible scales of internal vs state assessments). Its denominator is count_scored, NOT count_assigned, so multiplying this rate by count_assigned overstates the proficient count, badly on the sources where many rows carry no verdict. Pair it with count_scored, which is the n it rests on. Built from additive primitives (_sum_proficient / count_scored) so pre-aggregations roll it up to any grain.
measures.name: student_assessment_scores_view.pct_proficient
measures.title: Student Assessment Scores View Pct Proficient

measures.description: Proficiency rate across all formative module types (Quick Assessments, Multiple-Choice Quick Questions, and Constructed Response Questions). CRQ is included and also available as the standalone pct_proficient_crq measure. The denominator excludes rows with no proficiency verdict (is_mastery unset), matching pct_proficient. Built from additive primitives so pre-aggregations roll it up.
measures.name: student_assessment_scores_view.pct_proficient_formative
measures.title: Student Assessment Scores View Pct Proficient Formative

measures.description: Proficiency rate for Constructed Response Questions (CRQ) across all regions. CRQ is a subset of pct_proficient_formative. The denominator excludes rows with no proficiency verdict (is_mastery unset), matching pct_proficient. Built from additive primitives so pre-aggregations roll it up.
measures.name: student_assessment_scores_view.pct_proficient_crq
measures.title: Student Assessment Scores View Pct Proficient Crq

measures.description: Grain: recomputes at any query grain, but meaningful only within a single subject/standard — pooling percent-correct across assessments is a silent-failure trap (numerically valid, semantically meaningless). Average percent correct, internal-effective (null for state), built from additive primitives so pre-aggregations roll it up.
measures.name: student_assessment_scores_view.avg_percent_correct
measures.title: Student Assessment Scores View Avg Percent Correct

measures.description: Grain: recomputes at any query grain, but meaningful only within a single assessment source/subject/grade — scale scores are not comparable across sources, so pooling them is a silent-failure trap (numerically valid, semantically meaningless). Average scale score, built from additive primitives so pre-aggregations roll it up.
measures.name: student_assessment_scores_view.avg_scale_score
measures.title: Student Assessment Scores View Avg Scale Score
